notes: Optional: the reporter is the standalone extension Package components/herdr, which works on its own in plain PiG without this Piglet.

The extension does nothing unless PiG runs inside a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1 with HERDR_PANE_ID and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH set), as herdr-pig's does. It talks to herdr's socket as herdr-pig does (source pig); the herdr binary need not be on PATH.

With herdr 0.9.2 or later it also reports the resume command `pig --session <session file>` (or the session id), so herdr restores the pig session in its pane after a server restart. The restore runs plain `pig` (no Piglet or launch flags). Older herdr keeps the state reports and the release; it ignores the resume command.

It is a Go extension on PiG's public SDK: building the Piglet needs a Go toolchain, not Node.js. It also honors the herdr:blocked event on pi.events, through the Go SDK's bridge, as herdr-pig does. Setting PIGPEN_HERDR_UI_PROMPTS=1 also reports `blocked` while a PiG dialog is open (off by default: Pi has no such event and herdr-pig never reports one).

A local Piglet Binary builds with the reviewed PiG and reports to a fake herdr, but none is signed or published. The manifest lists five build targets, but only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.

Ported from herdr-pig (https://github.com/Hai-Fai-Solutions/herdr-pig) by Christian Polzer and Hai-Fai Solutions, Apache-2.0: the reporter's behavior, proven against the unmodified original (components/herdr/port/PORT.md), and the herdr plugin in herdr-plugin/ (herdr plugin install MichaelKinsy/pigpen/piglets/herdr/herdr-plugin). Their LICENSE and NOTICE ship beside that code.
